newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian silver prices held back by rising arrivals.
newsitem.headline: Indian silver prices held back by rising arrivals.

text.p: ** Indian 24 carat gold opens steady on Thursday at 4,590
** Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 grammes) steady at
53,700 rupees after losing 100 rupees on Wednesday.
** Silver (.999) starts 25 rupees lower at 6,725 rupees per
kg as fresh arrivals prompt offerings by stockists.
Indian 24 carat gold on Thursday opened steady at 4,590 rupees per 10 grammes against the previous close on limited arrivals while physical offtake was at a low ebb, dealers said.
Gold was down by 10 rupees per 10 grammes on Wednesday.
"Reports of a narrow fluctuation in the world market also kept local prices quiet in early trade," one broker said.
Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 grammes) opened steady at 53,700 rupees per piece after losing 100 rupees on Wednesday.
Silver (.999) opened 25 rupees lower at 6,725 rupees per kg against the previous close of 6,750 rupees amid fresh arrivals of the imported silver.
Weak world market trends also subdued local sentiment in early trade. Dealers said the Bombay market had received about 800/1,000 kg of imported silver on Thursday.
